line: Lenovo ThinkPad T14s Gen 7 (2026, Intel Panther Lake)
config_name: ThinkPad T14s Gen 7 — Core Ultra 7 365 vPro, 32GB LPDDR5X, 1TB SSD, 14" 2.8K 120Hz matte OLED

specs.keyboard_notes: ThinkPad keyboard 1.5mm travel, TrackPoint, auto backlit, fingerprint reader

battery.notes: 58Wh. IPS sibling measured ~17.5h Wi-Fi (NBC); OLED option costs ~15-25% runtime per NBC's note on higher panel consumption.

price.notes: Intel OLED CTO tier est. from verified AMD prebuilt $2,269 + OLED/vPro uplift (~US$2,450 US equivalent × ~1.35). Lenovo CA eCoupon volatility applies.

offers.name: Lenovo ThinkPad T14s Gen 7 Intel Laptop, 14", Intel Core Ultra 7 365 vPro, 32GB, 1TB SSD

reviews.quote: Lenovo also offers a matte 120 Hz 2.8K OLED panel if you prefer better image quality (but probably with higher power consumption).
Both the AMD and Intel SKUs offer pretty much the same level of performance.

praises: X1 Carbon-grade matte 2.8K 120Hz OLED at a meaningful discount to the X1 Carbon itself
vPro + native Thunderbolt 4 on the Intel board — the docking/management choice for IT fleets
Intel BE211 Wi-Fi 7 at 320 MHz: NBC measured ~3.9 Gbps on the Intel sibling, double the AMD card
OLED HDR (1100-nit peaks) finally makes video on a ThinkPad s worth watching
Same 58Wh battery and replaceable SSD/battery/WWAN as the rest of the line
complaints: OLED shaves 1.5-2.5h off the class-leading IPS battery (NBC flagged higher consumption)
Configurator price balloons past $3,000 CAD quickly — close to X1 Carbon territory
Soldered RAM caps out at 32GB on this prebuy tier
Matte OLED can show slight green tint at low grey levels (common on this panel family)
Static-UI burn-in caution for all-day spreadsheet users over 3-5 year ownership

design_philosophy: The Intel flagship display tier: the X1 Carbon's signature matte OLED transplanted into the cheaper, more repairable T14s chassis with vPro manageability — the pragmatic road-warrior pick when OLED is mandatory but flagship pricing is not.
rating_notes: Inferred from Notebookcheck's T14s Gen 7 AMD review (90%): OLED panel swap → screen_quality 9, readability_dark 9, creative_work +2, battery −1h (NBC note). Intel Ultra 7 365 ≈ AMD AI 7 PRO 450 per NBC's cross-platform note; gaming 3.0 for the 4-8 Xe3 iGPU (weaker than Radeon 860M per sibling benchmarks). Price estimated.
